examples.question_text: A bakery sells muffins in three packs: $4$ for $\$2.20$, $6$ for $\$3.18$ and $10$ for $\$5.40$. Determine the best buy by comparing prices per muffin. Do not round your answers.
examples.solution_text:
Pack of four:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$2.20}{4\text{ muffins}} &= \frac{\$0.55}{1\text{ muffin}}\end{align*}$
Pack of six:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$3.18}{6\text{ muffins}} &= \frac{\$0.53}{1\text{ muffin}}\end{align*}$
Pack of ten:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$5.40}{10\text{ muffins}} &= \frac{\$0.54}{1\text{ muffin}}\end{align*}$
The pack of six has the lowest price per muffin, so it is the best buy. The largest pack is not the best value.

examples.question_text: Coffee is sold in a $250$ g jar for $\$2.10$ and a $0.6$ kg jar for $\$4.80$. Which is the best buy?
examples.solution_text:
Convert both masses to kilograms.
$250\text{ g}=0.25\text{ kg}$
Small jar:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$2.10}{0.25\text{ kg}} &= \frac{\$8.40}{1\text{ kg}}\end{align*}$
Large jar:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$4.80}{0.6\text{ kg}} &= \frac{\$8.00}{1\text{ kg}}\end{align*}$
The $0.6$ kg jar has the lowest price per kilogram, so it is the best buy.

examples.question_text: Chips are sold in a $60$ g bag for $\$2.50$ and a $180$ g bag for $\$7.20$. Find the grams per dollar for each bag. Alex chooses the smaller grams-per-dollar value. Explain the mistake and state the best buy.
examples.solution_text:
Small bag:
$\begin{align*}\frac{60\text{ g}}{\$2.50} &= \frac{24\text{ g}}{\$1}\end{align*}$
Large bag:
$\begin{align*}\frac{180\text{ g}}{\$7.20} &= \frac{25\text{ g}}{\$1}\end{align*}$
Grams per dollar measures how much you get for the same money. The higher value is better, so Alex should choose the $180$ g bag.

examples.question_text: Bread rolls are sold in packs of $4$ for $\$2.60$ and packs of $6$ for $\$3.72$. Compare the cost of exactly $12$ rolls from each option and state the best buy.
examples.solution_text:
Packs of four:
$\begin{align*}\text{Number of packs} &= 12\div4\\&=3\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Cost} &= 3\times\$2.60\\&=\$7.80\end{align*}$
Packs of six:
$\begin{align*}\text{Number of packs} &= 12\div6\\&=2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Cost} &= 2\times\$3.72\\&=\$7.44\end{align*}$
Both options provide $12$ rolls. The packs of six cost less for that quantity, so they are the best buy.

examples.question_text: A shop sells two $1.25$ L bottles of lemonade for $\$4.75$, or a pack of $8\times300$ mL cans for $\$4.80$. Which is the best buy?
examples.solution_text:
Find the total volume of each offer.
$\begin{align*}\text{Bottle volume} &= 2\times1.25\text{ L}\\&=2.5\text{ L}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\text{Can volume} &= 8\times300\text{ mL}\\&=2400\text{ mL}\\&=2.4\text{ L}\end{align*}$
Compare prices per litre.
Bottles:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$4.75}{2.5\text{ L}} &= \frac{\$1.90}{1\text{ L}}\end{align*}$
Cans:
$\begin{align*}\frac{\$4.80}{2.4\text{ L}} &= \frac{\$2.00}{1\text{ L}}\end{align*}$
The bottles have the lowest price per litre, so they are the best buy.

examples.derivation: Independently calculated 2.20 ÷ 4 = 0.55, 3.18 ÷ 6 = 0.53 and 5.40 ÷ 10 = 0.54 dollars per muffin. The six-pack is cheapest per muffin. Matches Book 4 Development Q7(a), with changed values.

250 g = 0.25 kg. Independently calculated 2.10 ÷ 0.25 = 8.40 and 4.80 ÷ 0.6 = 8.00 dollars per kilogram. The 0.6 kg jar is better value. Matches Book 4 guided practice (c), using common units before comparison.

Independently calculated 60 ÷ 2.50 = 24 and 180 ÷ 7.20 = 25 grams per dollar. Higher quantity for the same dollar means better value, so the 180 g bag wins. The mistake explanation matches Book 4 Mastery Q9–10.

For 12 rolls, independently calculated 12 ÷ 4 = 3 packs costing 3 × 2.60 = 7.80 dollars; 12 ÷ 6 = 2 packs costing 2 × 3.72 = 7.44 dollars. Six-packs cost less for the same quantity. Matches Book 4 Development Q7(b–c).

Independently calculated bottle volume 2 × 1.25 = 2.5 L and can volume 8 × 300 = 2400 mL = 2.4 L. Unit prices are 4.75 ÷ 2.5 = 1.90 and 4.80 ÷ 2.4 = 2.00 dollars per litre. Bottles are better value. Matches the bundle comparison in Book 4 Mastery Q11 and attached image14.png.
